Path 1, policyGOALS §2

Falco

Runtime detection: what happened after admission said yes.

WHAT IT IS

A CNCF Graduated runtime security tool that watches syscalls and Kubernetes audit events via eBPF and alerts on rules: a shell in a container, an unexpected Secret read, a ConfigMap edited outside Argo.

WHAT SETS IT APART

Detection, not prevention. Versus Tetragon: Falco has the larger rule library; Tetragon can enforce in-kernel. Either covers the gap admission policy leaves.

WHERE WE STAND

Trial on one cluster with one out-of-band-change rule first.

"After Admission: Kernel Enforcement for Agents Kyverno Let In", KubeCon NA 2026

TRIAL

Falco: Runtime detection: what happened after admission said yes. Where we stand: Trial on one cluster with one out-of-band-change rule first. The one rule worth writing first: alert on any write to a Secret or ConfigMap that didn't come from Argo CD's service account.
